claim: In SQLite, write-ahead logging means readers never block writers, therefore SQLITE_BUSY errors cannot occur.

A.title: SQLite: enable WAL mode and busy_timeout for concurrent write performance · Issue #907 · cashubtc/nutshell
A.text:
- The default SQLite journal mode (delete) serializes all writes and readers block on writers.
- Using PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL allows concurrent reads during writes.
- Using PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000 waits for locks at the driver level instead of failing immediately.

B.title: SQLite Error: Database Is Locked (Fix Guide)
B.text:
- SQLite's database is locked means another connection holds a write lock and yours gave up waiting.
- SQLite allows one writer at a time.
- Enabling WAL mode (PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL) stops readers from blocking the writer.
- Setting a busy timeout (PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000) makes a short-lived conflict wait instead of failing instantly.
